answer: Idena's proof-of-personhood gates each seat on solving human-made "flip" puzzles inside one synchronized global window: scrambled picture-stories that only a real mind can reorder. Because every validation fires in the same brief window, a fleeting comet of time, one operator can attend only a single session, so N agents demand N humans solving at once. An AI farm fumbling the flips is as obvious as yarrow passed off as lotus, and clones never earn the verified-human badge a seat requires. The scarce cost is real simultaneous people, not copies.
